lines.japanese: 今朝の冷え込みは、１２月に入ってから一番のものだった。
lines.english: This was the coldest morning since December began.

lines.japanese: マフラーをいつもより強く絞って、今日もハイソな住宅展示場の中を歩いていく。
lines.english: I cinched my scarf tighter than usual and once again set out through the upscale model-home development.

lines.japanese: 僕の中で水曜日っていうのはそんなに重要な位置を占めていない。
lines.english: Wednesday had never occupied a particularly important place in my life.

lines.japanese: まあ、週の真ん中のこの曜日を好きなひとっていうのも、不動産の会社のひとくらいしか思いつかないんだけど。
lines.english: Then again, the only people I could imagine feeling any affection for the middle of the week were real-estate agents.

lines.japanese: でも、朝から頭の中を自由に使える時間が一番多いのも水曜日かもしれない。月曜日は前の日のことばかり考えてしまうし、金曜日は次の日のことでいっぱいだ。
lines.english: Still, Wednesday might be the morning when my thoughts had the most freedom to wander. On Mondays, I could think of nothing but the day before; on Fridays, my mind was already full of the day to come.

lines.japanese: そういえば、近頃冬の空や景色を意識することが少なくなった。何か別段変わったことがあるわけじゃないんだけど、こうして見渡してみるのが僕は好きだったはずだ。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I had paid less and less attention lately to the winter sky and scenery. Nothing in particular had changed, but I was sure I used to enjoy looking around me like this.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 空を見上げようとした矢先、耳よりも下の位置から聞こえる声に、意識を地上に戻した。冬の空に馴染んだ水色のスモックの上に、黄色い帽子だけが鮮やかだ。
lines.english: Just as I was about to raise my eyes to the sky, a voice from somewhere below my ears called my attention back to earth. Against a pale-blue smock that blended into the winter sky, only a yellow cap shone bright.

lines.japanese: 「あ、やさしいおにいちゃんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, it's the nice big brother.”

lines.japanese: 小さな手が伸びて、自転車に乗った若い女性の裾をくいくいと引っぱった。
lines.english: A tiny hand reached up and tugged twice at the hem of a young woman sitting astride a bicycle.

lines.japanese: 「あら、誰かのお兄ちゃん？」
lines.english: “Oh? Somebody's big brother?”

lines.japanese: 母親と呼ばれた彼女は、娘と僕の顔を交互に見比べて、にこにこと穏やかな微笑を浮かべる。ゆったりとした雰囲気の中で、彼女の足だけが自転車のペダルを忙しく逆回転させていた。
lines.english: The woman the child called Mother looked from her daughter’s face to mine with a mild, unhurried smile. Amid all that calm, only her feet were busy, spinning the bicycle pedals backward.

lines.japanese: 僕はその母親の真似をして笑顔を作ると、下にいる女の子に向かって手を上げた。彼女は黄色い帽子のようにぱっと顔を明るくして、遠慮がちに小さな手を横に振る。
lines.english: I copied the mother's smile and raised a hand to the little girl below. Her face lit as brightly as her yellow cap, and she gave me a small, timid wave.

lines.japanese: 「いってきます」
lines.english: “I'm off!”

lines.japanese: 母親はそれに対する言葉を待ちきれないとばかりに、僕に向かって深く頭を下げて、彼女の背中をとんとんと突付いた。その笑顔はやっぱりにこにこと穏やかだった。
lines.english: As though she could not bear to wait for my answer, the mother bowed deeply and gave her daughter a few pats on the back. Her smile remained as mild and serene as ever.

lines.japanese: 僕は一声かけようかと思ったけど、１２月の空は事なかれ主義だと知っていたから、その場でいってらっしゃいとだけ呟いて歩きはじめた。
lines.english: I thought about calling something after them. But I knew the December sky preferred that no one make a fuss, so I merely murmured, ‘Have a good day,’ where I stood and began walking again.

lines.japanese: 壁のない道路の真ん中をゆっくりと。
lines.english: Slowly, down the middle of a road without walls.

lines.japanese: 「各駅停車・柳木原行き、ドア閉まりまーす」
lines.english: “Local service for Yanagihara. Doors closing.”

lines.japanese: 「お荷物、お体、お引きください」
lines.english: “Please keep yourselves and your belongings clear of the doors.”

lines.japanese: 背中からどどっと人の波に押され、僕は入ってきたドアとは反対側のドアに押しつけられた。
lines.english: A great surge of bodies struck me from behind and pressed me against the doors opposite the ones I had entered through.

lines.japanese: それでも、真ん中辺りで吊り革もつかめずに立っているよりはましだ。僕は体重をドアに預けながら、足元の位置関係だけを気にしていた。
lines.english: Even so, it was better than standing in the middle without so much as a strap to hold. Resting my weight against the doors, I concentrated only on the arrangement of the feet around mine.

lines.japanese: その小さな配置図の中に、想定外の物体が割りこんできた。面ではなく点。一本の細い棒切れだった。
lines.english: Something unexpected intruded upon that tiny diagram. Not a surface, but a point: one slender stick.

lines.japanese: 僕はなんとか体を捻じまげて、自分の背後にあるシルバーシートを振りかえる。こひゅっと呼吸が出て、声がうまく出なかった。せめて、身体がもう少し後ろを向けばしゃべれるのに。
lines.english: I managed to twist around and look toward the priority seats behind me. My breath escaped in a little gasp, and my voice refused to work. If only I could turn a little farther, I might be able to speak.

lines.japanese: 「あのっ、杖ついてるひとが……」
lines.english: “Excuse me—there's someone with a cane...”

lines.japanese: 「つえ、ついてるひとがいるんで、だれか替わって……」
lines.english: “There's someone with a cane. Could somebody please give up their—”

lines.japanese: 自分の声よりも電車の走行音の方が耳に入ってくる。他のひとに僕の声が届かないのは明らかだった。
lines.english: The clatter of the train reached my ears more clearly than my own voice. Plainly, no one else could hear me.

lines.japanese: 僕はままならない下半身はそのまま、上半身を９０度ほど捻って声を出した。
lines.english: Leaving my trapped lower body where it was, I twisted my torso nearly ninety degrees and tried again.

lines.japanese: 「あの、誰か――」
lines.english: “Excuse me, could someone—”

lines.japanese: 「どうぞ」
lines.english: “Please, take my seat.”

lines.japanese: 突然、僕の背後からひとの気配が消えて、隣の密集地に隙間が出来た。
lines.english: All at once, the presence behind me vanished, and a pocket of space opened in the crush beside us.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございます」と、６０代くらいの女性の声が聞こえる。何故かその声は、電車の走行音に邪魔されずによく聞こえた。
lines.english: A woman who sounded as though she was in her sixties said, “Thank you.” For some reason, her voice came through clearly, untouched by the noise of the train.

lines.japanese: よかった、親切なひとが替わってあげたんだ。
lines.english: Good. Someone kind had given her the seat.

lines.japanese: 僕はその見えないひとに感謝した。それと同時に、そのひとにもいいことがありますようにと祈った。
lines.english: Silently, I thanked that unseen person. At the same time, I prayed that something good would happen to them in return.

lines.japanese: 「すごい体勢してるね」
lines.english: “That's quite a pose you've got there.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: その親切なひとは山科さんだった。
lines.english: The kind person was Yamashina.

lines.japanese: 「やなぎはらー、やなぎはらー」
lines.english: “Yanagihara. Yanagihara.”

lines.japanese: 「終点ー、柳木原です。お忘れ物ないようご注意ください」
lines.english: “This is the final stop, Yanagihara. Please take care not to leave any belongings behind.”

lines.japanese: 自動改札を抜けると、ようやく１２月の外気を実感できた。山科さんは小さく、僕は大きく、冬の空気を肺の中へと吸いこんでいく。
lines.english: Only after we passed through the ticket gates did the December air truly reach us. Yamashina drew a small breath and I a deep one, filling our lungs with winter.

lines.japanese: 「おはよ」
lines.english: “Morning.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、おはよう」
lines.english: “Yeah. Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 僕たちは同じ電車の同じ車両の同じ場所にいたのに、ほとんど話をしなかった。
lines.english: We had occupied the same place in the same car of the same train, yet had scarcely spoken.

lines.japanese: 理由として、一つには満員電車の中で話がしづらかったこと。もう一つはあまりに体が密着しすぎていて、お互いに口数が減っていったからだ。
lines.english: For one thing, conversation was difficult on a packed train. For another, our bodies had been pressed so close together that neither of us had found much to say.

lines.japanese: 「え、えっと」
「電車が一緒になるのは初めてかもね」
lines.english: “I think that's the first time we've ridden the same train.”

lines.japanese: 僕が車内での悶々とした気持ちを引きずって、次に出す言葉を考えていたら、山科さんに先を越されてしまった。
lines.english: Still carrying the turmoil of the ride inside me, I was searching for what to say next when Yamashina beat me to it.

lines.japanese: 「そういえばそうかも。同じ駅の同じ車両に乗ってたんなら、駅で会ってもよかったのにね」
lines.english: “Now that you mention it, I think you're right. If we use the same station and the same car, you'd think we might have met on the platform before.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　でも山科さん座ってなかった？　風見ヶ丘から乗ってよく座れたね」
lines.english: “Wait. Weren't you sitting down? You did well to find a seat after boarding at Kazamigaoka.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん私、始発駅から乗ってきたから」
lines.english: “No. I got on at the first stop.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、始発？」
lines.english: “The first stop?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Mm-hm.”

lines.japanese: 始発って、風見ヶ丘始発の電車はないはずだから、わざわざ逆方向に一度向かったってことになる。どうしてそんなことしたんだろう。
lines.english: No trains originated at Kazamigaoka, which meant she had deliberately ridden in the wrong direction first. Why would she do that?

lines.japanese: というよりも、そこまでして座るなら、シルバーシートなんか選ばなければいいのに。
lines.english: More to the point, if she had gone that far to get a seat, why choose one of the priority seats?

lines.japanese: 「誰かに譲りたかったんだ」
lines.english: “I wanted to give it to someone.”

lines.japanese: 僕の考えを見通したかのように、山科さんは説明を補足した。つまり、彼女としてはこの状況は想定内――
lines.english: As though she had read my thoughts, Yamashina supplied the explanation. So from her perspective, everything had gone according to plan—

lines.japanese: 「羽田君が居たのは予想外だったけど」
lines.english: “I didn't expect you to be there, though.”

lines.japanese: ――でもなかったみたいだ。
lines.english: —or perhaps not.

lines.japanese: 「え、でも、どうしてそんなことするの。普通に立っていけばいいじゃない」
lines.english: “But why go to all that trouble? You could simply have stood from the beginning.”

lines.japanese: 「んー？」
lines.english: “Hmm?”

lines.japanese: がくんと頭が傾いて、山科さんはしばらく考えた。
lines.english: Her head tipped abruptly to one side, and she considered the question for a while.

lines.japanese: 「誰かに感謝されたいときってない？」
lines.english: “Don't you ever have days when you want somebody to thank you?”

lines.japanese: 「感謝？」
lines.english: “Gratitude?”

lines.japanese: 「そう、感謝。途中経過はどうであれ『ありがとう』って言われたいとき」
lines.english: “Yes. Days when, however you get there, you want to hear someone say 'thank you.'”

lines.japanese: 「え、それはあるけど、それなら最初から席に座らなければいいんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Well, yes. But if that was the point, couldn't you simply have left the seat empty?”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ」
lines.english: “Hee hee.”

lines.japanese: 「あれっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: どうして山科さんは笑ったんだろう。今のって面白い部分だったのかな。
lines.english: Why had Yamashina laughed? Had I said something funny?

lines.japanese: 「羽田君すごいなあ。それが正しい考え方なんだろうね」
lines.english: “You're remarkable, Haneda. I suppose that must be the proper way to think about it.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、どういうこと？」
lines.english: “What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「つまり私の場合『ありがとう』の言葉が欲しかったってことかな」
lines.english: “I suppose what I wanted was the words themselves: 'thank you.'”

lines.japanese: 「言葉じゃなくてもとにかく感謝されればそれでいいって言うかー、例えばチラシ配りのひとがチラシを誰にも受けとってもらえなかったら、いらなくてももらったり」
lines.english: “Or maybe the gratitude is enough even without the words. Say somebody is handing out flyers and no one will take one. I'll accept it even if I don't want it.”

lines.japanese: 「あと駅前に立って募金をやってたら、喜んで入れるね。無人の募金箱には入れないけど、ひとがやってたら『ありがとう』が聞けるから」
lines.english: “And if someone is collecting donations outside the station, I'll gladly give. I wouldn't put money in an unattended collection box, but if a person is there, I get to hear 'thank you.'”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: そういうのは分かる気がする。感謝されることは対人関係において一番楽だ。
lines.english: I thought I understood. Being thanked was the easiest kind of human connection.

lines.japanese: 「そういうこと。ちょっと極端でも、とにかく『ありがとう』が欲しい日があるの」
lines.english: “That's what I mean. Even if it seems a little extreme, some days I simply need a 'thank you.'”

lines.japanese: 「でも良いことしてるのには変わりないよね？　だったらそれも正しい考え方なんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “But you're still doing something good, aren't you? Then maybe your way of thinking is right too.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ、そうかも」
lines.english: “Hee hee. Maybe so.”

lines.japanese: 「きっと山科さんの元にもいいことが訪れると思うよ」
lines.english: “I'm sure something good will find its way to you too.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、綺麗な言葉」
lines.english: “Ahaha. What pretty words.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そ、そうかな」
lines.english: “D-do you think so?”

lines.japanese: 確かにひとに優しくすればいいことが返ってくるなんて、子供みたいな発想だ。僕の歳になって言うことじゃないかもしれない。
lines.english: It was a childish idea, certainly: be kind to others and good things will happen to you. Perhaps I was too old to say such things.

lines.japanese: 「ま、いいことあったけど」
lines.english: “Still, something good did happen.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、いつ？」
lines.english: “What? When?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、いま」
lines.english: “Hmm... just now.”

lines.japanese: 「いま？」
lines.english: “Just now?”

lines.japanese: いつだろう。僕の知らない間に、山科さんは空に虹でも見たんだろうか。
lines.english: When had that been? Had Yamashina glimpsed a rainbow while I wasn't looking?

lines.japanese: 「おれは気づかなかったけど、やっぱりいいことって巡ってるもんなんだね」
lines.english: “I didn't notice, but I suppose good things really do come back around.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだといいね」
lines.english: “I hope they do.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうだよ。おれも一日に一つはいいことが出来るといいな」
lines.english: “They do. I hope I can do one good thing every day myself.”

lines.japanese: 「ていうか羽田君の場合、いつも他のひとにいいことがあるように願ってて……」
lines.english: “But in your case, Haneda, you're always wishing for good things to happen to everyone else...”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは僕の方を見てなにか言いかけたけど、すぐに俯いてしまった。
lines.english: Yamashina looked at me and began to say something more, only to lower her eyes almost at once.

lines.japanese: 「……いっか」
lines.english: “...Never mind.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、なにが？」
lines.english: “Huh? Never mind what?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、羽田君にはいいことあると思うよ」
lines.english: “Nothing. I think something good will happen to you, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんはそう言ったけど、僕のためにそう言ってくれる彼女が、幸せになればいいなと思った。
lines.english: That was what Yamashina said. But I found myself hoping that she—the girl who could say such a thing for my sake—would find happiness.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: あ、針生さんだ。
lines.english: Oh, Hariu.

lines.japanese: 駅構内のフラワーショップの前にいる僕たちを見て、針生さんがゆっくり近づいてきた。
lines.english: Seeing us beside the flower shop inside the station, Hariu slowly approached.

lines.japanese: 同じ制服の僕たちが駅で会うということは、少なくとも学校までは一緒に向かうことを意味する。
lines.english: When students in the same uniform met at the station, it meant they would at least travel together as far as school.

lines.japanese: 針生さんがそのことを厭わずに、声をかけてくれることが嬉しかった。
lines.english: I was glad Hariu did not mind that prospect and had chosen to speak to us.

lines.japanese: 「針生さん。おはようございます」
lines.english: “Good morning, Hariu.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ羽田かァ、ちょうどいい、俺もおまえに話があったんだ」
lines.english: “Ah, Haneda. Good timing. There's something I wanted to discuss with you.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは鞄からペットボトルを取りだしながら、僕の目の前に立った。
lines.english: Hariu stopped before me as he took a plastic bottle from his bag.

lines.japanese: 「一限目ちょっと付き合え。二人で話がしたい」
lines.english: “Come with me during first period. I want to talk, just the two of us.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: 朝からとんでもないことを言うひとだ。僕は授業を休んだことはあっても、さぼったことは一度もない。
lines.english: What an outrageous thing to suggest first thing in the morning. I had missed class before, but I had never once cut it.

lines.japanese: 針生さんは驚く僕を見ながら、ペットボトルの中身をぐいっと一気に煽った。
lines.english: Watching my astonishment, Hariu tipped up the bottle and drained it in one long swallow.

lines.japanese: 「行ってくれば？」
lines.english: “Why don't you go?”

lines.japanese: 「だ、駄目だよそんなの。授業を休むなんて出来ないよ」
lines.english: “I-I can't do that. I can't simply skip class.”

lines.japanese: 「んー……そう？」
lines.english: “Hmm... Can't you?”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは頬に手を当てて、小さく顔を傾けた。
lines.english: Yamashina laid a hand against her cheek and tipped her face slightly.

lines.japanese: 「お勉強よりもやることがあるなら、そっちを優先して何が悪い。まあ、強制は出来ないけどなァ」
lines.english: “If you’ve got something more important to do than study, what’s wrong with giving it priority? Still, I can’t force you.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ええと……」
lines.english: “No, um...”

lines.japanese: 「ちっ、乾く……」
lines.english: “Tch. Dry again...”

lines.japanese: 針生さんがペットボトルを逆さにしたけど、もう中の液体は残っていなかった。続けて鞄の中も探るけど、ストックはないようだった。
lines.english: Hariu turned the bottle upside down, but not a drop remained. He rummaged through his bag next, apparently finding no spare.

lines.japanese: 「まあおまえがそう言うなら仕方ない。じゃあまたあとでお会いしましょう、ファッキン委員長」
lines.english: “Well, if you insist, it can’t be helped. Until later, then, you fucking class president.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは身を翻すと、体を駅の出口へと向けた。だけどその出口は、僕たちが向かうべき出口とは逆の方向だった。
lines.english: Hariu wheeled around and headed for an exit—but it was the one opposite the way we needed to go.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれっ、どこに行くんですか、そっちは学校じゃありませんよ」
lines.english: “W-wait. Where are you going? School isn't that way.”

lines.japanese: 「コンビニ。水が切れた」
lines.english: “Convenience store. I'm out of water.”

lines.japanese: 本当は一緒に学校まで行きたかったけど、仕方ないか。僕はもう一人の同行者候補である山科さんの方を見た。
lines.english: I had wanted to walk to school with him, but that couldn't be helped. I looked to Yamashina, my other prospective companion.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ。私も欲しいものがあったんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, that's right. There's something I need too.”

lines.japanese: だけど彼女も、何か用事を思いだしたみたいで、針生さんと同じ方向に体を向けてしまった。
lines.english: But she too seemed to remember an errand, and turned in the same direction as Hariu.

lines.japanese: うーん、せっかくみんなと登校できると思ったのに、ちょっと寂しいな。
lines.english: Hmm. I had thought I would finally get to school with everyone. It was a little lonely.

lines.japanese: 「なに買いに行くの？　おれも付き合うよ」
lines.english: “What are you going to buy? I'll come with you.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、ちょっと距離が離れてるからいい。遅刻するかも」
lines.english: “Hmm, no, it’s a bit far. You might be late.”

lines.japanese: 「俺はコンビニに暇つぶしがあれば一限は休む。なんなら、付き合うか」
lines.english: “If the convenience store has anything good for killing time, I'm skipping first period. You're welcome to join me.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんの買い物にも興味があるし、針生さんの話というのも確かめたかったけど、授業料を叔父さんと叔母さんが出してくれてることを考えると、やっぱり休んだり出来ない。
lines.english: I was curious about Yamashina's errand, and I wanted to know what Hariu wished to discuss. But when I remembered that my aunt and uncle paid my tuition, I knew I couldn't skip class after all.

lines.japanese: 「すみません、おれはやっぱり授業には出ます」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I think I had better go to class.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか、それもいいだろ」
lines.english: “I see. That’s a fine choice too.”

lines.japanese: 「またあとでね」
lines.english: “See you later.”

lines.japanese: 一緒に学校に行けないのは残念だけど、こうして話が出来ただけでも楽しかったし、またいつか一緒になることもあるだろう。
lines.english: It was disappointing that we couldn't walk to school together, but I had enjoyed this brief conversation. Surely there would be another chance someday.

lines.japanese: 学校とは逆の出口に向かう二人を、僕はときどき振りかえって見送った。
lines.english: I watched them depart through the exit away from school, glancing back several times as I went.

lines.japanese: 駅で二人と話した時間分、僕は学校まで小走りで向かうことになった。
lines.english: To make up for the time I had spent talking with them at the station, I had to jog to school.

lines.japanese: 冬に走ると喉に空気がへばりついて、咳をするのも苦しくなる。針生さんみたいにミネラルウォーターが欲しい。
lines.english: When you run in winter, the air clings to your throat until even coughing hurts. I wanted a bottle of mineral water like Hariu's.

lines.japanese: ふうと息をついて膝に手を当てた。僕の脇を学園の生徒たちが通りすぎていく。
lines.english: I breathed out and braced my hands on my knees. Students streamed past me toward the school.

lines.japanese: クラスのひとを何人か見かけたけど、僕に声をかけるひとは一人も居なかった。
lines.english: I spotted several people from my class, but not one of them spoke to me.

lines.japanese: 「ふうッ」
lines.english: “Hah!”

lines.japanese: もう一度大きく息を吐いて、僕は呼吸を整えた。よし、ここまで来たらもう走らなくても大丈夫だ。ぱしんと小さく顔を叩いて、校門の中へ足を踏みいれる。
lines.english: I let out one more great breath and steadied my breathing. Good. From here, I no longer needed to run. I gave my cheeks a light slap and stepped through the school gates.

lines.japanese: その僕の横を、長い髪をなびかせてクラスのひとが通りがかった。いや、クラスのひとっていうかあれは……。
lines.english: Just then, someone from my class passed beside me, long hair streaming behind her. Or rather, not merely someone from my class. That was...

lines.japanese: 「あっ」
lines.english: “Oh!”

lines.japanese: 「わ、渡来さん！」
lines.english: “W-Watarai!”

lines.japanese: 振りかえってはくれなかったけど、彼女は僕の声に、その場でぴたと足を止めた。
lines.english: She didn't turn around, but at the sound of my voice she stopped dead where she stood.

lines.japanese: よかった、喉に空気がへばりついてるから、声が小さくならないか心配したけど、聞こえたみたいだ。
lines.english: Good. With the cold air clinging to my throat, I had worried my voice might come out too faint, but she seemed to have heard.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: とっさに挨拶をしてみたものの、昨日持ちあがった不安が頭をよぎる。もしかして避けられてたりしたらどうしよう。
lines.english: The greeting came out on impulse, only for yesterday's unease to cross my mind. What if she really had begun avoiding me?

lines.japanese: 「あ、聞こえなかったかな。渡来さん、おはよう」
lines.english: “Oh, did you not hear me? Good morning, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 返事がなかったので、僕はしつこく食いさがった。
lines.english: When no answer came, I stubbornly pressed her for one.

lines.japanese: ん？　んん？
lines.english: Hm? Hmm?

lines.japanese: いま声が聞こえた気がするけど、なんだろう……何か言ったぞ。僕は彼女に近づいてみた。
lines.english: I thought I had heard her voice just now. What was it...? She had definitely said something. I went closer.

lines.japanese: 「あれ、いま何か言ったのかな、渡来さん……」
lines.english: “Did you say something just now, Watarai...?”

lines.japanese: 耳を寄せてみたものの、やっぱり聞きとれなかった。
lines.english: Even when I leaned in, I still couldn't make it out.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、聞こえないよ」
lines.english: “Sorry, I can't hear you.”
“G'morning.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、もうちょっと大きい声で……」
lines.english: “Watarai, could you say it a little louder...?”

lines.japanese: 僕はさらに一歩近づいた。すると、それまで俯いていた渡来さんがぐりんと振りむいた。
lines.english: I stepped closer still. Watarai, who had been staring at the ground all this time, whipped around.
“What. Did. You. Say?”

lines.japanese: 「えええっ」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: 意味が分からない。朝の挨拶をしただけなのに、どうして怒られなくちゃいけないんだろう。僕はぽかんと口を開くことしか出来なかった。
lines.english: I didn't understand. I had only wished her a good morning. Why did that deserve her anger? All I could do was stand with my mouth hanging open.

lines.japanese: 「用がないなら先に行くね」
lines.english: “If that's all, I'm going on ahead.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、用っていうか、挨拶したかっただけなんだけど……」
lines.english: “Huh? It wasn't anything in particular. I only wanted to say good morning...”

lines.japanese: 「ふっ」
lines.english: “Heh.”

lines.japanese: 今度は笑われた。怒ったり笑ったり渡来さんも大変だ。彼女は一度深呼吸をすると、今日会ってから、ようやくと笑顔を見せてくれた。
lines.english: Now she was laughing at me. It must be hard work, getting angry and laughing by turns. She took one deep breath, then finally smiled at me for the first time that morning.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「お、おはよう」
lines.english: “G-good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ先に行くね」
lines.english: “I'll go on ahead, then.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、そうじゃなくて、他にも話したいことが……」
lines.english: “No, wait. There was something else I wanted to talk about...”

lines.japanese: 追いかけようとしたけど、僕が昇降口で上履きに履き替えようともたついている間に、彼女の姿を見失ってしまった。
lines.english: I tried to follow, but while I fumbled with my indoor shoes at the entrance, she disappeared from sight.

lines.japanese: でもよかった、避けられてなくて。
lines.english: Still, thank goodness. She wasn't avoiding me.

lines.japanese: 「なにあんた、明日香さまに愛想つかされたの」
lines.english: “What, has Lady Asuka finally gotten sick of you?”

lines.japanese: 「あ……高内さん、おはよう」
lines.english: “Oh... Good morning, Takauchi.”

lines.japanese: シンデレラ階段の前で高内さんに会った。何だろう、今日は機嫌がいいみたいだ。
lines.english: I met Takauchi at the foot of the Cinderella Stairs. For some reason, she seemed in a good mood today.

lines.japanese: そういうときの高内さんは声が大きいので、僕は言葉尻がすぼんでしまった。
lines.english: When she was like this, her voice tended to be loud. Mine dwindled to nothing by the end of the sentence.

lines.japanese: 「え、だあーってぇー、なんかいまガン無視されてなかった？　それなのに追っかけるって、おまえどんだけしつけーんだよ」
lines.english: “Whaaat? Wasn’t she totally ignoring you just now? And you still went chasing after her? How freaking clingy can you get?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、違うんだよ、渡来さんは急いでるって言ってたんだ。だから挨拶が出来なくてさ」
lines.english: “No, that's not what happened. Watarai said she was in a hurry. She just didn't have time for a greeting.”

lines.japanese: 「へーえ、さっき、そこでのんびり岡村としゃべってたけど？」
lines.english: “Really? She was standing right over there having a nice, leisurely chat with Okamura a minute ago.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、じゃあ、岡村さんに用事があったんじゃないかな。二人とも仲がいいみたいだし」
lines.english: “Oh. Then perhaps she needed to speak to Okamura. They do seem to be good friends.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃなくておまえ、まーた待ちあわせブッチこいたんじゃねーの。あんたさあ、ほんと時間とか約束みたいなん守んねーじゃん」
lines.english: “That’s not the point. You stood her up again, didn’t you? Seriously, you never show up on time or keep your promises.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないと思うけど……おれ、約束を破ったことなんてないし……」
lines.english: “I don't think that's true... I've never broken a promise...”

lines.japanese: 「うそつけ」
lines.english: “Liar.”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは吐きすてるように何か言ったけど、僕にはその音がよく聞こえなかった。
lines.english: Takauchi spat something under her breath, but I couldn't quite catch it.

lines.japanese: 「ま、あんたがそう言うならそれでもいいけどぉー？　元々、おまえには高嶺の花だったっつー話でしょ」
lines.english: “Well, if that's your story, fine by me. She was always out of your league anyway, right?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、渡来さんは美人だよね」
lines.english: “Yes. Watarai really is beautiful.”

lines.japanese: 「マジうぜー……」
lines.english: “God, you're annoying...”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは話の途中で行ってしまった。あとを追おうかとも思ったけど、上履きの具合が悪い気がして、位置を直していたら遅れてしまった。
lines.english: Takauchi walked off in the middle of our conversation. I considered following her, but something felt wrong with my indoor shoe. By the time I adjusted it, I had fallen behind.

lines.japanese: それにしても、僕と渡来さんの様子を心配してくれた高内さんはいいひとだ。彼女の声が落ちついているときにでも、声をかけてみよう。
lines.english: Still, it was kind of Takauchi to worry about how things stood between Watarai and me. I would try talking to her sometime when her voice was calmer.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.
